page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, alongside 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 caches. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware included with this instance type, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in specific single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. The server achieves strong results in gzip compression at 35.73 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.74 GB/sec single-threaded and 204.86 GB/sec multi-threaded. It also demonstrates strong static web serving throughput at 54.55 GB/sec. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the instance delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 362.36 tokens/sec and strong prompt processing speeds of 2835.04 tokens/sec. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Passmark, place the server in the average tier, with a Passmark CPU score of 48774.22 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 31811.54.

The primary tradeoff of the D32ls_v7 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications or large in-memory databases. However, this configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive RAM allocations, allowing users to access high-frequency Intel Xeon cores without paying for unused memory. Supported by advanced vector and matrix extensions, this server is well-suited for compute-bound tasks, web serving, lightweight machine learning inference, and data compression pipelines.
